'''Golriz Ghahraman''' ({{langx|fa|گلریز قهرمان}}; born 1981) is a New Zealand former politician and lawyer. The former United Nations lawyer was a child [[asylum seeker]], and became the first [[refugee]] elected to [[New Zealand Parliament|New Zealand's Parliament]].<ref name=Johnston>{{cite news |title=Meet Golriz Ghahraman, the Green Party's newest Member of Parliament |first=Kirsty |last=Johnston |url= http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11898165 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=7 October 2017 |access-date=28 November 2017}}</ref> Ghahraman was a member of the [[New Zealand House of Representatives]] for the [[Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand|Green Party]] from 2017 to 2024, when she resigned amid multiple shoplifting allegations, which she was later convicted of.

==Early life and education==
Ghahraman was born in [[Iran]] in 1981.<ref name=metro>{{cite news |title=Barrister and Green Party candidate Golriz Ghahraman |first=Francis |last=Morton |date=29 June 2017 |access-date=20 April 2018|work=[[Metro (magazine)|Metro]]|url=https://www.pressreader.com/new-zealand/metro-magazine-nz/20170629/281629600284813|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180422202058/https://www.pressreader.com/new-zealand/metro-magazine-nz/20170629/281629600284813|archive-date=22 April 2018}}</ref> Her family lived in [[Mashhad]], Iran's second largest city, where her father, an agricultural engineer, worked for the Ministry of Agriculture on the research and development of plant-based [[alternative fuel]]s.<ref name=Johnston/> Her mother studied as a child psychologist but was ethically opposed to "psychologists having to pledge allegiance to a religion" so refused to sit the Islamic examinations required for her to practise and never worked as such.<ref name=Vernon>{{Cite web |url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/88498722/green-lawyer-hopes-to-be-first-refugee-to-win-a-seat-in-parliament |title=Green lawyer hopes to be first refugee to win a seat in Parliament |last=Small|first=Vernon|date=17 January 2017|website=[[Stuff.co.nz|Stuff]] |access-date=22 January 2017}}</ref><ref name="day in the life">{{cite news |title=A day in the life of Green Party candidate Golriz Ghahraman |first=Britt |last=Mann |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/95236850/a-day-in-the-life-of-green-party-candidate-golriz-ghahraman |work=[[Stuff.co.nz|Stuff]] |date=5 August 2017 |access-date=10 March 2018}}</ref> Her father was [[Shia]] and her mother a [[Kurdish people|Kurdish]] [[Sunni]], though neither parent was religious.<ref name=Vernon/>

In 1990, following the end of the [[Iran–Iraq War]], nine-year-old Ghahraman and her family left Iran for Malaysia, ostensibly for a holiday.<ref name="majorityrule">{{cite news |title="We Can't Rely on Majority Rule": Meet NZ's First Refugee MP |quote=Golriz Ghahraman on how escaping Iran's oppressive regime and defending war criminals in international courts has shaped her politics.|last1=McClure |first1=Tess |last2=Taylor|first2=Laura |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/we-cant-rely-on-majority-rule-meet-nzs-first-refugee-mp/ |work=[[Vice Media|Vice]] |date=10 October 2017 |access-date=30 March 2018}}</ref> From Malaysia they booked flights to Fiji, with a stopover in Auckland, where they sought political asylum and were accepted as refugees. Her parents later set up a restaurant and a gift shop in Auckland and did not work in their earlier areas of expertise.<ref name=Vernon/>

Ghahraman attended [[Auckland Girls' Grammar School]].<ref name="aggs">{{cite web|url=http://aggs.school.nz/images/2016/October_2016.pdf|title=Auckland Girls' Grammar School Newsletter Issue 09/16|website=aggs.school.nz|publisher=[[Auckland Girls' Grammar School]]|date=21 October 2016|access-date=20 April 2018|archive-date=22 April 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180422202515/http://aggs.school.nz/images/2016/October_2016.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> She has a [[Bachelor of Laws]] and Bachelor of Arts in history from the [[University of Auckland]],<ref name="lawtalk912">{{cite news |title=Human rights lawyer vows to defend the defenceless |first=Craig |last=Stephen |url=https://www.lawsociety.org.nz/news-and-communications/people-in-the-law/lawyer-profiles/human-rights-lawyer-vows-to-defend-the-defenceless |work=LawTalk |publisher=[[New Zealand Law Society]] |date=3 November 2017 |access-date=12 March 2018 |archive-date=9 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200809181703/https://www.lawsociety.org.nz/news-and-communications/people-in-the-law/lawyer-profiles/human-rights-lawyer-vows-to-defend-the-defenceless |url-status=dead }}</ref> and a [[Master of Studies]] (MSt) degree in International Human Rights Law with Distinction from the [[University of Oxford]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ihrlmst.conted.ox.ac.uk/|title=Master's in International Human Rights Law – Master in International Human Rights Law (LLM alternative)|publisher=University of Oxford|access-date=3 April 2018|archive-date=4 April 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180404230306/http://ihrlmst.conted.ox.ac.uk/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Professional life==

Ghahraman entered legal practice in New Zealand working as a [[Barrister#New Zealand|junior barrister]] specialising in criminal defence, describing it as "the most frontline human rights area of law you can work in practice {{not a typo|in |in}} New Zealand; every day you are applying the Bill of Rights Act and you're dealing with unlawful detention, searches and discrimination."<ref name="lawtalk912"/><ref name="linkedin">{{Cite web|url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/golriz-ghahraman-28aa9a17/ |title=Golriz Ghahraman – United Nations Consultant (International human rights, justice) – United Nations Office of Drugs and Crime – LinkedIn|date=28 November 2017|publisher=[[LinkedIn]] |access-date=12 March 2018}}</ref>

Ghahraman worked as a lawyer for the United Nations as part of both the defence and prosecution teams with the tribunals in Rwanda, Cambodia and The Hague.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Dastgheib |first1=Shabnam |last2=van Beynen |first2=Jack |title=Payback time: What refugees are really worth |url= http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/71978514/Payback-time-What-refugees-are-really-worth |access-date=7 October 2017 |work=[[The Sunday Star-Times]] |date=13 September 2015}}</ref> She had worked on tribunals such as the [[International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda]], volunteering as an intern; and was assigned to the defence team. Her work on the defence teams of accused and convicted war criminals such as [[Radovan Karadžić]] and [[Simon Bikindi]], has caused her controversy, although she has claimed transparency throughout.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Kirk |first1=Stacey |title=Golriz Ghahraman explains smiling photo with convicted genocide perpetrator |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/99335136/golriz-gharaman-explains-smiling-photo-with-convicted-genocide-perpetrator |access-date=8 October 2018 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=28 November 2017 }}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/99307462/green-mp-says-voters-not-misled-about-her-role-defending-alleged-rwandan-war-criminal|title=Green MP says voters not misled about her role defending alleged Rwandan war criminal|website=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=28 November 2017 |access-date=28 November 2017}}</ref><ref name=quin>{{cite news |title=The Green MP and the genocide hearings |first=Phil |last=Quin |url= https://www.newsroom.co.nz/2017/11/27/63852/the-green-mp-and-the-genocide-hearings |work=[[Newsroom (website)|Newsroom]] |date=28 November 2017 |access-date=28 November 2017}}</ref>

Ghahraman returned to New Zealand in 2012 and worked as a barrister, specialising in human rights law and criminal defence. She appeared before the [[Supreme Court of New Zealand]] in a case which ultimately led to the police overhauling their rules about undercover operations.<ref>{{cite news |title=Drug convictions quashed by Supreme Court |url= http://www.radionz.co.nz/news/regional/292119/drug-convictions-quashed-by-supreme-court |access-date=21 October 2017 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=14 December 2015}}</ref><ref name="NZSC 189">{{cite NZLII |litigants="Wilson v R" |court=NZSC |year=2015 |num=189 |parallelcite=[2016] 1 NZLR 705 |date=14 December 2015 |courtname=auto}}</ref>

Ghahraman was selected as a Green party list candidate in January 2017 for the [[2017 New Zealand general election|2017 general election]]. She was ranked at eight on the Green party list and contested the [[Te Atatū (New Zealand electorate)|Te Atatū]] electorate, where she won 1,413 votes and placed fourth.<ref name="2017 Te Atatū">{{cite web |title=Official Count Results – Te Atatū |url=http://electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2017/electorate-details-53.html |access-date=23 December 2017 |publisher=New Zealand Electoral Commission |location=Wellington}}</ref> On the provisional results on election night the Greens did not attain a high enough party vote for Ghahraman to enter Parliament, though a slight increase for the Greens in the special vote saw her allocated a seat.<ref name="special votes">{{Cite web|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/97204595/greens-rely-on-special-votes-to-get-golriz-ghahraman-into-parliament|title=Greens rely on special votes to get Golriz Ghahraman into Parliament |last=Tokalau|first=Torika|date=25 September 2017|website=[[Stuff.co.nz]]|access-date=25 September 2017}}</ref> After the Greens gained 0.5% of the vote in special votes she was duly elected to Parliament, in so doing becoming New Zealand's first refugee MP.<ref>{{cite news|title = New Zealand election: full results give Labour boost and nation its first refugee MP|first = Eleanor|last = Ainge Roy|date = 7 October 2017|access-date = 8 October 2017|work= [[The Guardian]]|url = https://www.theguardian.com/world/2017/oct/07/new-zealand-election-full-results-labour-boost-and-first-refugee-mp}}</ref> Her maiden speech, delivered on 15 November 2017, detailed Ghahraman's refugee story and subsequent career as a human rights lawyer.<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 November 2017 |title=Address in Reply; Golriz Ghahraman |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/document/HansS_20171115_062400000/ghahraman-golriz |access-date=16 May 2024 |website=New Zealand Parliament}}</ref>[https://www.greens.org.nz/golriz-ghahraman-maiden-speech]

In November 2017, it was revealed that, along with prosecuting war criminals, Ghahraman had also volunteered as an intern for the legal defence team of accused war criminals such as [[Radovan Karadžić]], as part of her work with the [[United Nations]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite news|url=http://www.radionz.co.nz/news/political/344871/green-mp-under-scrutiny-for-role-in-rwandan-genocide-trials|title=Green MP under scrutiny for role in Rwandan genocide trials|date=28 November 2017|work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |access-date=28 November 2017}}</ref> She defended her role in this work, claiming that her role was necessary to "maintaining a fair and robust trial process," that she was "proud to have been involved in that tradition of fair and transparent international justice," and that, given the choice, she would "do it again".<ref name=":2" />

Ghahraman was re-elected a Green Party list MP at the [[2020 New Zealand general election|2020 New Zealand election]] and [[2023 New Zealand general election]], ranked seventh on the list each time. She contested, unsuccessfully, the [[Mount Roskill (New Zealand electorate)|Mount Roskill]] electorate in 2020 and the [[Kelston (New Zealand electorate)|Kelston]] electorate in 2023, placing third in each behind their Labour Party incumbents.<ref>{{cite web |title=2020 General Election and Referendums – Official Result Successful Candidates |url=https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2020/successful-candidates.html |access-date=12 November 2020 |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Mt Roskill – Official Result |url=https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2020/electorate-details-25.html |access-date=12 November 2020 |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=3 November 2023 |title=2023 General Election: Successful candidates |url=https://electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/successful-candidates.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231117114239/https://electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/successful-candidates.html |archive-date=17 November 2023 |access-date=20 November 2023 |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Kelston – Official Result |url=https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/electorate-details-19.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231107025030/https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/electorate-details-19.html |archive-date=7 November 2023 |access-date=7 November 2023 |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]]}}</ref>

Ghahraman's portfolio responsibilities within the Green Party included foreign affairs, defence, and justice; she held those roles from 2017 to 2024. She also held responsibility for immigration (2017–2020), customs (2018–2020), ethnic communities (2020–2024) and refugees (2020–2024).<ref name="j822">{{cite web |title=Ghahraman, Golriz |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/mps-and-electorates/former-members-of-parliament/ghahraman-golriz/ |access-date=16 May 2024 |website=New Zealand Parliament}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=29 November 2023 |title=Greens unveil portfolio spokespeople |url=https://www.1news.co.nz/2023/11/29/greens-unveil-portfolio-spokespeople/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231128214920/https://www.1news.co.nz/2023/11/29/greens-unveil-portfolio-spokespeople/ |archive-date=28 November 2023 |access-date=23 February 2024 |work=[[1News]]}}</ref> She sat on the foreign affairs, defence, and trade committee during her entire parliamentary career.<ref name="j822" />

=== Electoral reform ===
Ghahraman was outspoken on electoral reform issues. In early March 2019, she submitted a member's bill, the Electoral (Strengthening Democracy) Amendment Bill, that proposed reforms to seven areas of the [[Electoral Act 1993]] including lowering the country's [[Electoral system of New Zealand|mixed member proportional]] (MMP) threshold from 5% to 4%, giving prisoners the right to vote, limiting the total amount of donations to political parties, banning foreign donations to political parties, allowing [[Māori people|Māori]] voters to [[Maori Electoral Option|switch electoral rolls at any time]], and lowering the voting age to 16 years.<ref>{{cite news |date=4 March 2019 |title=Green MP Golriz Ghahraman urges scrutiny of 'who controls purse strings of bigger parties' |url=https://www.radionz.co.nz/news/national/383868/green-mp-golriz-ghahraman-urges-scrutiny-of-who-controls-purse-strings-of-bigger-parties |access-date=12 March 2019 |publisher=[[Radio New Zealand]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=8 March 2019 |title=Jami-Lee Ross wants new rules around financial donations to political parties from foreigners |url=https://www.tvnz.co.nz/one-news/new-zealand/jami-lee-ross-wants-new-rules-around-financial-donations-political-parties-foreigners?variant=tb_v_1 |access-date=12 March 2019 |work=[[1News]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=21 May 2022 |title=Green MP Golriz Ghahraman calls for voting age to be lowered to 16 |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2022/05/green-mp-golriz-ghahraman-calls-for-voting-age-to-be-lowered-to-16.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220623202747/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2022/05/green-mp-golriz-ghahraman-calls-for-voting-age-to-be-lowered-to-16.html |archive-date=23 June 2022 |access-date=5 August 2022 |work=[[Newshub]]}}</ref> Deputy prime minister [[Winston Peters]] and Opposition leader [[Simon Bridges]] criticised Ghahraman's bill as opportunistic.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Small |first1=Zane |title=Golriz Ghahraman: 'We welcome waiting until after 2020 for any changes to MMP' |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2019/03/golriz-ghahraman-we-welcome-waiting-until-after-2020-for-any-changes-to-mmp.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190514163241/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2019/03/golriz-ghahraman-we-welcome-waiting-until-after-2020-for-any-changes-to-mmp.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=14 May 2019 |access-date=12 March 2019 |work=[[Newshub]] |date=6 March 2019}}</ref>

The Strengthening Democracy bill was drawn from the ballot in mid-May 2022. That August, [[Attorney-General (New Zealand)|Attorney-General]] [[David Parker (New Zealand politician)|David Parker]] expressed concern that the bill's proposed donation cap could potentially breach the right to free speech.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Coughlan |first1=Thomas |date=3 August 2022 |title=Government legal advice finds political donation caps may breach right to freedom of speech |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/government-legal-advice-finds-political-donation-caps-may-breach-right-to-freedom-of-speech/W7UWSBHFTFY4IJA3QDMVMZ47FI/?dicbo=v2-207ea77e58462884cf4f7177cce43ce7& |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220803232222/https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/government-legal-advice-finds-political-donation-caps-may-breach-right-to-freedom-of-speech/W7UWSBHFTFY4IJA3QDMVMZ47FI |archive-date=3 August 2022 |access-date=5 August 2022 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]]}}</ref> The bill was defeated at its first reading in September 2022.<ref name="d973">{{cite web |date=7 November 2017 |title=Electoral (Strengthening Democracy) Amendment Bill |url=https://bills.parliament.nz/v/6/5002b6a7-dad0-4ffb-a3c0-71a3b63c5bba |access-date=16 May 2024 |website=New Zealand Parliament}}</ref> Nonetheless, much of the proposals in the bill were progressed. The [[Sixth Labour Government of New Zealand|Labour–New Zealand First coalition government]] banned foreign donations in 2019 and [[Voting rights of prisoners in New Zealand|re-enfranchised of short-term prisoners]] in 2020;<ref name="RNZ_2020">{{cite web |last1=Scotcher |first1=Katie |date=25 June 2020 |title=Prisoner voting bill passes in chaotic night at Parliament |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/419769/prisoner-voting-bill-passes-in-chaotic-night-at-parliament |access-date=5 March 2022 |website=[[RNZ]] |language=en-nz}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=3 December 2019 |title=New Zealand bans foreign political donations amid interference concerns |url=http://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/dec/03/new-zealand-bans-foreign-political-donations-amid-interference-concerns |website=[[The Guardian]] }}</ref> the Labour majority government reformed the Māori electoral option in 2022 and introduced, but did not complete, legislation to lower the voting age for local government elections.<ref name="z5422">{{cite web |last=Neilson |first=Michael |date=15 November 2022 |title=Labour and National agree on Māori electoral law change |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/labour-and-national-agree-on-maori-electoral-law-change/Y452KF37WBFKTIJJQMT652IGYQ/ |access-date=16 May 2024 |website=[[The New Zealand Herald]] }}</ref><ref name="r232">{{cite web |last=Corlett |first=Eva |date=16 January 2024 |title=New Zealand government rejects Ardern-era bid to lower voting age |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/jan/16/new-zealand-government-voting-age-change-rejected-minimum-terms-parliament |access-date=16 May 2024 |website=[[The Guardian]] }}</ref>

===Shoplifting and resignation===
[[File:Golriz Ghahraman with Gerry Brownlee (cropped).jpg|thumb|Ghahraman with [[Gerry Brownlee]], then [[Speaker of the New Zealand House of Representatives|Speaker of the House]], in April 2024]]
On 10 January 2024, Ghahraman stood aside from her portfolios after being accused of shoplifting at Scottie's Boutique in [[Ponsonby, New Zealand|Ponsonby]].<ref>{{Cite news |first=Philip|last=Crump|date=10 January 2024 |title=Green MP Golriz Ghahraman stands aside from portfolios after being accused of shoplifting |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/green-mp-golriz-ghahraman-stands-aside-from-portfolios-after-being-accused-of-shoplifting/4W6WIBVHVZA2LBODLNFEEST5B4/ |access-date=10 January 2024 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |language=en-NZ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240111023051/https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/green-mp-golriz-ghahraman-stands-aside-from-portfolios-after-being-accused-of-shoplifting/4W6WIBVHVZA2LBODLNFEEST5B4/|archive-date=11 January 2024|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Crump |first=Philip |date=10 January 2024 |title=Green MP Golriz Ghahraman stands aside from portfolios after being accused of shoplifting |url=https://www.newstalkzb.co.nz/news/politics/green-mp-golriz-ghahraman-stands-aside-from-portfolios-after-being-accused-of-shoplifting/ |access-date=10 January 2024 |work=[[Newstalk ZB]] |language=en-nz|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240113165936/https://www.newstalkzb.co.nz/news/politics/green-mp-golriz-ghahraman-stands-aside-from-portfolios-after-being-accused-of-shoplifting/|archive-date=13 January 2024|url-access=subscription}}</ref> On 12 January, a second shoplifting allegation at Scottie's Boutique against Ghahraman was reported. Police later confirmed that they were investigating the first shoplifting incident, which occurred in late December 2023.<ref>{{cite news |title=Further allegation of shoplifting at Scotties emerges against Golriz Ghahraman |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2024/01/further-allegation-of-shoplifting-at-scotties-emerges-against-golriz-ghahraman.html |access-date=15 January 2024 |work=[[Newshub]] |date=12 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240112053819/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2024/01/further-allegation-of-shoplifting-at-scotties-emerges-against-golriz-ghahraman.html |archive-date=12 January 2024}}</ref> Green co-leaders [[James Shaw (New Zealand politician)|James Shaw]] and [[Marama Davidson]] said the party was aware of the shoplifting allegations. On 15 January, a Green party spokesperson said that Ghahraman had returned to New Zealand from an overseas trip that day.<ref>{{cite news |title=Green MP Golriz Ghahraman returns to NZ amid shoplifting claims |url=https://www.1news.co.nz/2024/01/15/green-mp-golriz-ghahraman-returns-to-nz-amid-shoplifting-claims/ |access-date=15 January 2024 |work=[[1News]] |publisher=[[TVNZ]] |date=15 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240115031023/https://www.1news.co.nz/2024/01/15/green-mp-golriz-ghahraman-returns-to-nz-amid-shoplifting-claims/ |archive-date=15 January 2024|url-status=live}}</ref> That same day, police said they were investigating a third shoplifting allegation involving Ghahraman at the Wellington-based boutique store Cre8iveworx in October 2023.<ref>{{cite news |last1=McConnell |first1=Glenn |title=Police investigating Golriz Ghahraman allegation – this time in Wellington |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/133561585/police-investigating-golriz-ghahraman-allegation--this-time-in-wellington |access-date=15 January 2024 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=15 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240115115958/https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/133561585/police-investigating-golriz-ghahraman-allegation--this-time-in-wellington |archive-date=15 January 2024|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 16 January 2024, Ghahraman announced her resignation as a member of parliament for the Green Party, effective 18 January.<ref>{{Cite news |last=McConnell |first=Glenn |date=16 January 2024 |title=Golriz Ghahraman resigns amid shoplifting accusations |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/133563837/golriz-ghahraman-resigns-amid-shoplifting-accusations |access-date=16 January 2024|work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240115234201/https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/133563837/golriz-ghahraman-resigns-amid-shoplifting-accusations|archive-date=15 January 2024|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://gazette.govt.nz/notice/id/2024-ps227 |title=Notice of vacancy in seat in House of Representatives |date=19 January 2024 |work=[[New Zealand Gazette]] |access-date=19 January 2024}}</ref> In her statement, Ghahraman said a mental health evaluation found that her behaviour was "not rational in any way" and was due to "an extreme stress response ... relating to previously unrecognised trauma." She said, "I am not trying to excuse my actions, but I do want to explain them. People should, rightly, expect the highest standards of behaviour from their elected representatives. I fell short. I’m sorry".<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.greens.org.nz/statement_from_golriz_ghahraman |title=Statement from Golriz Ghahraman |date=16 January 2024 |access-date=16 January 2024 |last=Ghahraman |first=Golriz |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240116053827/https://www.greens.org.nz/statement_from_golriz_ghahraman |archive-date=16 January 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref> Her place in Parliament was filled by [[Celia Wade-Brown]], a former [[Mayor of Wellington]], who was the next candidate on the Green Party's list at the 2023 election.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/golriz-gharahmans-replacement-who-is-celia-wade-brown/RZOJQ3FO5VF5NMTFLXJWU4PHT4/ |title=Golriz Gharahman's replacement: Who is Celia Wade-Brown? |date=16 January 2024 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |accessdate=17 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240117121628/https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/golriz-gharahmans-replacement-who-is-celia-wade-brown/RZOJQ3FO5VF5NMTFLXJWU4PHT4/|archive-date=17 January 2024|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 17 January, Police said Ghahraman had been charged with two counts of shoplifting and that investigations into the allegations were continuing.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Doyle |first1=Trent |last2=Mitchell |first2=Travis |title=Golriz Ghahraman charged with two counts of shoplifting |url= https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2024/01/police-still-investigating-former-green-mp-golriz-ghahraman-s-alleged-shoplifting-no-charges-laid.html |access-date=17 January 2024 |work=[[Newshub]] |date=17 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240117043622/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2024/01/police-still-investigating-former-green-mp-golriz-ghahraman-s-alleged-shoplifting-no-charges-laid.html |archive-date=17 January 2024}}</ref> On 23 January, Police announced a third shoplifting charge, relating to alleged offending at a Wellington retailer on 22 October 2023.<ref>{{cite news |title=Third charge laid after Golriz Ghahraman shoplifting claims |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/nz-news/350155497/police-lay-third-charge-over-golriz-ghahraman-shoplifting-allegations |access-date=25 January 2024 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=23 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240123182804/https://www.stuff.co.nz/nz-news/350155497/police-lay-third-charge-over-golriz-ghahraman-shoplifting-allegations|archive-date=23 January 2024|url-status=live }}</ref> In total, Ghahraman was accused of stealing $9978 worth of items under the three charges.<ref name="Newshub 4th charge">{{cite news |last1=Hewett |first1=William |title=Police reveal new shoplifting charge against ex-Green MP Golriz Ghahraman relates to new store |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2024/02/police-reveal-new-shoplifting-charge-against-ex-green-mp-golriz-ghahraman-relates-to-new-store.html |access-date=29 February 2024 |work=[[Newshub]] |date=27 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240228123435/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2024/02/police-reveal-new-shoplifting-charge-against-ex-green-mp-golriz-ghahraman-relates-to-new-store.html |archive-date=28 February 2024}}</ref>

On 27 February, ''[[Newshub]]'' reported that Ghahraman was facing a fourth shoplifting charge in relation to the theft of a cardigan valued at NZ$389 from [[Newmarket, New Zealand|Newmarket]] retailer Standard Issue.<ref name="Newshub 4th charge" /> On 13 March she pleaded guilty to all four charges.<ref>{{cite news | url= https://www.stuff.co.nz/nz-news/350210512/former-green-mp-golriz-ghahraman-pleads-guilty-shoplifting | title=Former Green MP Golriz Ghahraman pleads guilty to shoplifting |first=Caroline |last=Williams |date=13 March 2024 |access-date=13 March 2024 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240313035506/https://www.stuff.co.nz/nz-news/350210512/former-green-mp-golriz-ghahraman-pleads-guilty-shoplifting|archive-date=13 March 2024|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 27 June 2024, she was convicted of four charges of shoplifting and fined $1600 and court costs of $260. She was denied a discharge without conviction.<ref>{{Cite news |date=27 June 2024 |title=Former Green Party MP Golriz Ghahraman gets $1600 fine for shoplifting, denied discharge without conviction |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/new-zealand/2024/06/former-green-party-mp-golriz-ghahraman-gets-1600-fine-for-shoplifting.html |access-date=27 June 2024 |work=[[Newshub]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240627050927/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/new-zealand/2024/06/former-green-party-mp-golriz-ghahraman-gets-1600-fine-for-shoplifting.html|archive-date=27 June 2024|url-status=dead}}</ref> During an exclusive interview with [[TVNZ]] journalist [[John Campbell (broadcaster)|John Campbell]], Ghahraman described her shoplifting as acts of "self-sabotage" motivated by work-related stress and online bullying.<ref>{{cite news |title='Just shame, shame,' – Former MP Golriz Ghahraman speaks in first interview |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/520696/just-shame-shame-former-mp-golriz-ghahraman-speaks-in-first-interview |access-date=4 July 2024 |work=[[RNZ]] |date=27 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240701013752/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/520696/just-shame-shame-former-mp-golriz-ghahraman-speaks-in-first-interview |archive-date=1 July 2024|url-status=live}}</ref> In October 2024, Ghahraman appealed the four shoplifting convictions; her lawyer argued the convictions may impact Ghahraman's application for a job at the [[International Criminal Court]].<ref name="j551">{{cite web |last=Williams |first=Caroline |date=14 October 2024 |title=Former Green MP Golriz Ghahraman appeals shoplifting convictions |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/nz-news/350450133/former-green-mp-golriz-ghahraman-appeals-shoplifting-convictions |access-date=13 October 2024 |website=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] }}</ref> The request for a discharge without conviction was denied.<ref name="r775">{{cite web |last=Kapitan |first=Craig |date=20 October 2024 |title=Ex-Green MP Golriz Ghahraman loses appeal for $9k shoplifting spree, conviction to stand |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/crime/ex-green-mp-golriz-ghahraman-loses-appeal-for-auckland-wellington-shoplifting-spree/DCROI5WZD5GCBFCFHP56ZJUOQI/ |access-date=20 October 2024 |website=[[The New Zealand Herald]] }}</ref>

==Views and positions==
===David Seymour controversy===
In mid-May 2019, [[ACT New Zealand|ACT Party]] leader [[David Seymour]] sparked controversy with comments made during a radio interview, where he referred to Ghahraman as a "menace to freedom in [New Zealand]" and likened her views on [[hate speech]] to tactics used by [[Mao Zedong]], [[Joseph Stalin]], and [[Adolf Hitler]] to "gain power through the suppression of [[Freedom of speech|free expression]]". The statement drew immediate responses from all political sides of the [[New Zealand Parliament]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=12232004|title=Act leader David Seymour taken to task for Golriz Ghahraman comments|date=17 May 2019|work=[[The New Zealand Herald]]}}</ref>

===Human rights===
Ghahraman spoke out against United States President [[Donald Trump]]'s [[Executive Order 13769|travel ban]], saying in 2017: "I wouldn't travel to America right now. I wouldn't want to face what people are facing – held in handcuffs and being interrogated by security forces, [...] I wouldn't want that [border detention] for anyone."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nz.news.yahoo.com/top-stories/a/34299427/woman-aiming-to-be-nzs-first-refugee-mp-too-scared-to-go-to-us/#page1|title='Don't go': Woman aiming to be NZ's first refugee MP too scared to go to US|date=22 January 2017|website=[[Yahoo]]|access-date=30 January 2017}}</ref>

She believes representation for women and minorities in politics is important: "Ultimately the sinister face of populism is what really pushed me over the edge to run as a candidate.  The hate speech became scary. I knew that representation is important. I knew that to stop the very real attacks against minorities and women, we had to get really active, to support each other, and forge paths. We have to become leaders ourselves."<ref>{{cite web|last1=Golbakhsh|first1=Ghazaleh|title=How my friend Golriz is hoping to change the world|url=http://villainesse.com/girl-power/how-my-friend-golriz-hoping-change-world-one-step-time|website=Villainesse|access-date=1 April 2017|archive-date=22 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170322135631/http://www.villainesse.com/girl-power/how-my-friend-golriz-hoping-change-world-one-step-time|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In early March 2019, Ghahraman suggested that the New Zealand Government cooperate with any potential Kurdish and United Nations process to bring home captured New Zealand Jihadist [[Mark John Taylor]], who had joined the [[Islamic State]] in 2014.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Forrester |first1=Georgia |title='Kiwi jihadi' Mark Taylor: Should NZ help to bring him home? |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/111024951/kiwi-jihadi-mark-taylor-should-nz-help-to-bring-him-home |access-date=12 March 2019 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=5 March 2019}}</ref>

She was one of four women MPs from different political parties who co-sponsored legislation banning [[female genital mutilation in New Zealand]] in 2020.<ref name="n775">{{cite web |date=7 November 2017 |title=Crimes (Definition of Female Genital Mutilation) Amendment Bill |url=https://bills.parliament.nz/v/6/8083ec4d-5dfe-4ac2-98af-13e13c121f3c |access-date=16 May 2024 |website=New Zealand Parliament}}</ref>

===Israel–Palestine===
In mid-July 2019, Ghahraman was accused of [[anti-Semitism]] by New Zealand Jewish Council spokesperson Juliet Moses after she published a tweet on 11 July describing [[Mary, mother of Jesus|Mary]] and [[Saint Joseph|Joseph]] as [[Palestinians|Palestinian]] refugees. Moses alleged that Ghahraman was denying the Jewish connection to the land by not recognising [[Jesus]] was Jewish. Ghahraman apologised that her comments had offended the Jewish community, thanking the Jewish community for their support for refugees. A Green Party spokesperson responded that Golriz had apologised for her "poorly worded remarks" and said that Ghahraman was going to work with Jewish communities to improve dialogue.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Bhatia |first1=Ripu |title=New Zealand Jewish Council accuses Green Party MP of 'antisemitism' |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/114200033/new-zealand-jewish-council-accuses-green-party-mp-of-antisemitism |access-date=12 July 2019 |publisher=[[Stuff.co.nz]] |date=12 July 2019}}</ref> In response, left-wing blogger [[Martyn "Bomber" Bradbury]] defended Ghahraman and the Green Party from accusations of anti-Semitism, arguing that this was an attempt to deflect from [[Israeli-occupied territories|Israel's occupation of Palestinian land]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bradbury |first1=Martin |title=The Green Party are many things, antisemites are not one of them |url=https://thedailyblog.co.nz/2019/07/15/the-green-party-are-many-things-antisemites-are-not-one-of-them/ |website=The Daily Blog|access-date=16 July 2019 |date=15 July 2019}}</ref>

In December 2020, Ghahraman joined fellow Green MP [[Teanau Tuiono]] and [[New Zealand Labour Party|Labour]] MP [[Ibrahim Omer]] in pledging to form a new parliamentary Palestine friendship group to "raise the voices of Palestinian peoples in the New Zealand Parliament" during an event organised by the Wellington Palestine advocacy group to mark "International Day of Solidarity with the Palestinians".<ref>{{cite web |title=New Zealand MPs take pledge for Palestine |url=https://ppost24.com/post/978/new-zealand-mps-take-pledge-for-palestine |website=Palestine Post 24 |access-date=11 December 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201210132047/https://ppost24.com/post/978/new-zealand-mps-take-pledge-for-palestine |archive-date=10 December 2020 |date=9 December 2020}}</ref>

In response to the [[2021 Israel–Palestine crisis]], Ghahraman criticised what she regarded as the New Zealand Government's slow response in issuing a statement on the conflict. She also criticised Israel for encouraging "very violent systemic attacks" on the Palestinian population in [[East Jerusalem]] and bombarding [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Nixon |first1=Jane |title=Golriz Ghahraman condemns NZ Govt, says international humanitarian laws have been breached in Gaza conflict |url=https://www.tvnz.co.nz/one-news/new-zealand/golriz-ghahraman-condemns-nz-govt-says-international-humanitarian-laws-have-been-breached-in-gaza-conflict |access-date=17 May 2021 |work=[[1News]] |date=16 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210516131840/https://www.tvnz.co.nz/one-news/new-zealand/golriz-ghahraman-condemns-nz-govt-says-international-humanitarian-laws-have-been-breached-in-gaza-conflict |archive-date=16 May 2021|url-status=live}}</ref> In response, the New Zealand Jewish Council accused Ghahraman of misrepresenting the [[Sheikh Jarrah controversy|Sheikh Jarrah dispute]] and ignoring [[Palestinian rocket attacks on Israel|Hamas' rocket attacks on Israelis]], which in their view made her unfit to serve as the Greens' foreign affairs spokesperson.<ref>{{cite news |author1=New Zealand Jewish Council |title=Green Party MPs Use Hamas Slogan |url=https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO2105/S00169/green-party-mps-use-hamas-slogan.htm |access-date=21 May 2021 |work=[[Scoop (website)|Scoop]] |date=21 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210520063535/https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO2105/S00169/green-party-mps-use-hamas-slogan.htm |archive-date=20 May 2021|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 19 May, Ghahraman sponsored a motion calling for members of parliament to recognise the right of Palestinians to self-determination and statehood. The motion was supported by the Greens and the [[Māori Party]] but was opposed by the centre-right [[New Zealand National Party|National]] and ACT parties. The governing [[New Zealand Labour Party|Labour Party]] also declined to support the Greens' motion with the Speaker of the House [[Trevor Mallard]] criticising Ghahraman for sponsoring the motion despite knowing that it was going to be voted down.<ref name="RNZ Green Party motion">{{cite news |title= Green Party motion to call for recognition of Palestine's right to self-determination |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/442887/green-party-motion-to-call-for-recognition-of-palestine-s-right-to-self-determination |access-date=21 May 2021 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=19 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210520003402/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/442887/green-party-motion-to-call-for-recognition-of-palestine-s-right-to-self-determination |archive-date=20 May 2021|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Stuff Green Party motion">{{cite news |last1=Manch |first1=Thomas |title=Green Party's motion to declare Palestine a state fails in Parliament |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/125175638/green-partys-motion-to-declare-palestine-a-state-fails-in-parliament |access-date=21 May 2021 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=19 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210520053549/https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/125175638/green-partys-motion-to-declare-palestine-a-state-fails-in-parliament |archive-date=20 May 2021|url-status=live}}</ref>

In response to criticism by [[ACT New Zealand|ACT Party]] deputy leader [[Brooke Van Velden]], Ghahraman also defended fellow Green MP [[Ricardo Menéndez March]]'s tweet that said: "[[From the river to the sea]], Palestine will be free!" Ghahraman claimed that March was defending the rights of both Arabs and Jews to having equal rights in their homeland.<ref name="RNZ Green Party motion" />

In response to the [[Gaza war]], Ghahraman described the "scenes in Israel" as "heartbreaking". She stated that "Nothing justifies targeting or harming civilians. Palestinian armed groups and Israeli forces must make every effort to protect civilians now."<ref>{{cite news |title=NZ leaders respond to Gaza attacks |url=https://thespinoff.co.nz/live-updates/08-10-2023/nz-leaders-respond-to-gaza-attacks |access-date=10 October 2023 |work=[[The Spinoff]] |date=8 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231008042537/https://thespinoff.co.nz/live-updates/08-10-2023/nz-leaders-respond-to-gaza-attacks |archive-date=8 October 2023|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Religious beliefs ===
Ghahraman describes herself as "agnostic—some days I would say atheist", noting that "It was important for me to get up and say I'm actually not religious at all, because the Middle East also has diversity within it".<ref name=Vernon/><ref name=metro/>

== Personal life ==
Ghahraman has [[multiple sclerosis]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/119838474/green-mp-golriz-ghahraman-reveals-she-has-multiple-sclerosis|title=Green MP Golriz Ghahraman reveals she has multiple sclerosis|date=26 February 2020|website=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |language=en|access-date=26 February 2020}}</ref>

She was in a relationship with comedian [[Guy Williams (comedian)|Guy Williams]],<ref>{{Cite web|last=Mann|first=Britt|date=14 June 2020|title=Golriz Ghahraman on growing up, Guy Williams, and the power of protest|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/entertainment/books/300026616/golriz-ghahraman-on-growing-up-guy-williams-and-the-power-of-protest|access-date=14 June 2020|website=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |language=en}}</ref> which ended in late 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/life-style/sunday-magazine/people-ideas/300391970/hive-life-golriz-ghahraman-and-nicola-willis-open-up-about-sacrifices-and-motiviations |title=Hive life: Golriz Ghahraman and Nicola Willis open up about sacrifices and motiviations |date=5 September 2021 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |first=Glenn |last=McConnell}}</ref>

In June 2021, Ghahraman wrote that she was getting her first Kurdish [[Deq (tattoo)|deq]] tattoos, stating, "I could not be more excited to help revive this beautiful indigenous tradition and connect with the incredible proud elders I remember wearing theirs back home. They represent a pre-Islamic culture of strength, nature and the night sky."<ref name="Deq">{{cite news |last1=Small |first1=Zane |title=Green MP Golriz Ghahraman 'could not be more excited' about new tattoo embracing her Kurdish roots |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2021/06/green-mp-golriz-ghahraman-could-not-be-more-excited-about-new-tattoo-embracing-her-kurdish-roots.html |newspaper=[[Newshub]] |access-date=27 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210925120049/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2021/06/green-mp-golriz-ghahraman-could-not-be-more-excited-about-new-tattoo-embracing-her-kurdish-roots.html |archive-date=25 September 2021 |date=8 June 2021 |url-status=dead}}</ref>
